For the year ended December 31, 2024, we generated revenue of $894.4 million, a 2% decrease from $914.2 million of revenue for the year ended December 31, 2023.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text MD&A — verify whether the headline -2% revenue print accurately conveys the underlying segment dynamics, and whether the consolidated narrative obscures a segment that is collapsing.
rfm_tuples.M_value: U.S. Marketplace +13% ($647M -> $734M); Digital Wholesale -55% ($216M -> $98M); Other +23%. Within Digital Wholesale: Wholesale rev -49% ($101M -> $51M), Product rev -60% ($115M -> $47M), Transactions -47% (65,418 -> 34,395). Digital Wholesale segment income from operations: -$179.3M (vs -$96.4M in 2023). Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 5/8/2025, pre-cutoff): Wholesale -52%, Product -58% (continued deterioration).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosed (Mode A PASS), but the headline framing of '-2% revenue' is materially anodyne: the Digital Wholesale segment built around the 2021 CarOffer acquisition is in structural collapse (-55%, accelerating into Q1 2025 at -52%/-58%). The 'multi-product platform' thesis the 10-K maintains is being unwound in real time.

rfm_tuples.R: For the year ended December 31, 2024, we recognized Digital Wholesale segment impairment charges related to the CarOffer reporting unit of $127.5 million as impairment operating expense ... For the year ended December 31, 2024, we recognized Digital Wholesale segment impairment charges related to the CG Buy Online reporting unit of $9.8 million and $7.0 million as wholesale cost of revenue and impairment operating expense, respectively.
rfm_tuples.f: claim_evolution — compare CarOffer impairment-risk language across 10-K (Feb 2024), Q1 2024 10-Q (May 2024), Q2 2024 10-Q (Aug 2024); did the company telegraph the impairment or did the triggering event come abruptly?
rfm_tuples.M_source: claim_evolution via self_text on 4 sequential filings (10-K FY23, 10-Q Q1/Q2/Q3 2024)
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K FY23 (Feb 2024) and Q1 2024 10-Q (May 2024) both flagged that 'the excess of the fair value over the carrying value declined for the CarOffer reporting unit' as of the 10/1/2023 annual test, and warned a future impairment 'could be material'. Q1 2024 explicitly stated 'we did not identify any triggering events' for the three months ended 3/31/2024. By Q2 2024 (June 30, 2024 — triggering event date), they recognized $127.5M of impairment. Wholesale revenue trajectory through 2024 quarters: -36%, -59%, -44%, then -52% in Q1 2025. CG Buy Online pilot terminated Oct 31, 2024, contributing additional $16.8M of impairment.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The CarOffer goodwill cushion was disclosed as thin in early 2024 — so the impairment is not a hidden surprise (PASS on prior-period warning). Severity is Moderate because (a) CarOffer was a $375M+ acquisition in 2021 plus Dec-2023 $75M minority buyout, now impaired by $127.5M with FV-over-carrying still narrow at 10/1/2024, leaving 'risk for future impairment charges if projected future operating results further decline' — and Q1 2025 wholesale -52% suggests the new fair value is also under pressure. The CG Buy Online pilot termination represents a second failed digital-retail bet inside one fiscal year.

rfm_tuples.R: During the year ended December 31, 2024, we repurchased and retired 6,357,302 shares for $146.1 million ... at an average cost of $22.98 per share under the 2024 Share Repurchase Program. On November 7, 2024, we announced that our Board of Directors authorized the 2025 Share Repurchase Program pursuant to which we may, from time to time, purchase shares of our Class A common stock for an aggregate purchase price not to exceed $200.0 million.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text Q1 2025 10-Q — verify pace and timing of 2025 buybacks vs cash burn; cross-reference with founder insider sales.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 financing activities: $184.2M of share repurchases at $31.12 avg price (vs $32.90 close 2025-05-15), consuming 92% of the $200M 2025 authorization in a single quarter. Cash dropped from $304.2M to $172.9M between YE2024 and 3/31/2025 (a -43% / -$131M decline in one quarter). Simultaneously, founder/Exec Chair Langley Steinert sold $43.5M of stock between Dec 16, 2024 and May 9, 2025 via a Rule 10b5-1 plan from a family trust; monthly insider sale proceeds across all officers stepped from <$1.5M/month before Nov 2024 to ~$10M/month Dec 2024-Feb 2025.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding. Disclosure exists (PASS on existence of buyback program and 10b5-1), but capital allocation pattern is telling: the company is sprinting through its 2025 authorization in Q1 at $31/share — supporting the market while the controlling shareholder is the most active personal seller. The buyback is mechanically transferring cash from corporate balance sheet to the controlling holder's family trust at $28-30/share. Not illegal; 10b5-1 affirmative defense documented. But the framework reads this as 'insider liquidity event funded by corporate buyback in the same months', which is a textbook value-extraction pattern in companies with structural top-line headwinds.

rfm_tuples.R: Because of the ten-to-one voting ratio between our Class B and Class A common stock, Langley Steinert, our founder and Executive Chair, is able to exercise voting rights with respect to a majority of the voting power of our outstanding capital stock. More than 50% of our voting power is held by Mr. Steinert and certain of his affiliates and we are therefore a 'controlled company' under Nasdaq rules.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text — verify dual-class structure and 'controlled company' status; cross-check with form4 to confirm the founder is converting Class B (10 votes) to Class A and selling.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Confirmed dual-class with 10:1 voting ratio; founder controls >50% of voting power. CarGurus is a Nasdaq 'controlled company' and elects exemptions from independent-board majority requirements. Form 4 data shows Steinert's Class A sales are from 'The Langley Steinert Irrevocable Family Trust dated June 21, 2004' — i.e., conversions of his super-voting block into salable Class A shares are flowing through estate-planning vehicles. The transfer-on-sale provision in the charter converts Class B to Class A upon disposal, so each $1 of insider sale also dilutes his voting power eventually.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosed (Mode A PASS). Mode B: governance structure creates an unbalanced agency dynamic — the controlling holder personally captures value via buybacks at $28-31 while public shareholders bear the post-CarOffer impairment and segment-collapse risk. The fact that the family trust is the systematic seller, while the company simultaneously runs $184M of buybacks in Q1 alone, is structurally similar to fading-conviction founder exits seen in other Boston tech (cf. legacy 'controlled company' insider distribution patterns).

The framework treats this as MODERATE because (a) it is structurally disclosed; (b) 10b5-1 footnotes are present; (c) the issuer is not in distress; but (d) the cluster pattern + buyback coincidence is exactly the 'controlling holder fading conviction' signal the framework was built to capture.

summary: CARG is a solvent, GAAP-profitable marketplace platform whose 10-K honestly discloses the structural collapse of the 2021 CarOffer wholesale acquisition ($127.5M Q2 2024 goodwill impairment, plus $16.8M for the abandoned CG Buy Online pilot — $144.4M total). Liquidity, audit, and litigation pillars all PASS: $304M cash, $390M undrawn revolver, no debt, E&Y since 2016 with unqualified opinion, no material litigation, no customer concentration, paying-dealer base growing. The four MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY findings are Mode B narrative/disclosure-tone gaps rather than fraud: (1) the '-2% revenue' headline obscures Digital Wholesale -55%; (2) Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 5/8/2025) shows wholesale/product still deteriorating at -52%/-58%, putting the residual CarOffer carrying value at fresh risk despite the 10/1/2024 'FV > carrying' test; (3) capital-allocation pattern in Q1 2025 — $184M buyback at $31/share alongside $43.5M of founder 10b5-1 sales from his family trust — is a textbook controlled-company value-extraction overlay; (4) insider monthly sale pace stepped 8-10x from Nov 2024 onward. Verdict: NEUTRAL with a mild SHORT-tilt. The honesty filter does not exclude CARG — disclosure quality is reasonable and balance sheet is fine — but the combination of a structurally collapsing segment, a controlled-company governance structure, and a buyback-funded insider-distribution pattern means the framework would not put this in a LONG basket.
